task.description: Diagnose and design a fix for the BLOCKER step-10-elixir-dev.json reported: provision_via_shared_connection/1's on_exit/1 teardown callback (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:303) reuses the caller's ambient Letflow.Repo connection, but ExUnit runs on_exit callbacks after the original test process has already exited, so the {:shared, self()} (or :auto, single-owner) connection that teardown/2 needs is gone by the time it runs, raising ** (exit) shutdown: "owner ... exited" from inside schema_present?/1 (via log_teardown/3 -> guarded/2), uncaught because both guarded/2 and log_teardown/3's rescue clauses only catch raise, never exit. Confirmed pre-existing on commit c38dfa9b (not caused by this rework's own §11.9 tenant_template.ex reorder), reproduced independently on backfill_test.exs (0/5, all 5 failing in teardown) and context_test.exs (5/11, 6 failures, identical shape).
acceptance_criteria: Design states precisely why provision_via_shared_connection/1's on_exit teardown fails today, re-derived from source (Sandbox/DBConnection.Ownership semantics, ExUnit's on_exit lifecycle), not merely restating the BLOCKER's claim

Design states whether teardown's DROP SCHEMA/delete_all statements need the SAME connection provisioning used, or merely a live connection with adequate visibility/permissions to the same database -- answered from teardown/2's own body, not asserted

Design specifies a concrete fix: routing provision_via_shared_connection/1's on_exit teardown through Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo (via the existing with_provisioning_repo/1 helper), while leaving provisioning itself on the caller's own shared connection (preserving §11.2's read-visibility fix, the reason this whole rework exists)

Design re-verifies this fix does not reopen the ORIGINAL ISS-0113/ISS-0480 hazard (a Sandbox.mode/2 call reaching Letflow.Repo's shared pool) or Mechanism 4 (§9.2/§11.9, a mid-sequence Sandbox.mode/2 call disrupting an in-flight caller connection)

Design addresses whether guarded/2 and log_teardown/3's rescue-only failure boundaries should be widened to also catch :exit, per INV-F-10's own stated intent, and explains why (or why not) teardown/2's own load-bearing DROP/DELETE statements should NOT be wrapped in the same boundary

Design specifies verification beyond 'the test suite is green': an explicit post-teardown check that the schema was actually dropped and the tracking rows actually deleted, not merely that ExUnit reported no failure
Signatures/structure only -- no implementation code (.ex bodies)

result.summary:
Diagnosed the BLOCKER independently (re-derived from Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox's and DBConnection.Ownership's own documented lifecycle plus ExUnit's own documented on_exit/1 ordering, not inherited from ELIXIR-DEV's report alone -- confirms the same conclusion). Root cause: provision_via_shared_connection/1's on_exit/1 closure (tenant_fixture.ex:303) reuses whatever connection is ambient for the CALLING process, but by the time ExUnit actually runs that callback, the calling process is a NEW on_exit process, not the original {:shared, self()} owner -- DBConnection.Ownership.Manager has no record of the new process as an owner/allowed process for that now-invalidated shared connection, so the first Repo.query!/2 inside teardown/2's call chain (schema_present?/1, reached via log_teardown/3 -> guarded/2) raises `exit, shutdown: "owner ... exited"`, uncaught because rescue does not catch exit (a distinct BEAM primitive from raise) -- confirmed via source reading of the relevant clauses, not assumption. Also found: this is actually TWO defects, not one -- (1) the connection itself is unusable from on_exit's process (root cause), and (2) guarded/2's rescue-only boundary cannot see exit at all, which independently violates INV-F-10's own stated intent on the diagnostic read path -- fixing only (2) would NOT fix the BLOCKER, since teardown/2's own unprotected DROP SCHEMA/delete_all statements aren't behind any guarded/2 boundary and would still raise the same exit.

Answered the dispatching handoff's own question directly, from teardown/2's unchanged body: its three statements (schema_name_for_tenant/1 lookup, DROP SCHEMA CASCADE, two delete_all calls) all key off a tenant_id already known before teardown runs -- none require visibility into a specific in-flight, uncommitted transaction. Committed rows are visible from any connection to the SAME Postgres database, and Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo already targets the identical database (config/test.exs: same `letflow_test#{MIX_TEST_PARTITION}`) as Letflow.Repo, just a separate pool -- confirmed by direct re-read of config/test.exs and provisioning_repo.ex, not assumed. So teardown does NOT need the same connection provisioning used; it needs a live, permissioned connection to the same database, which ProvisioningRepo already supplies, unconditionally, via the existing with_provisioning_repo/1 helper -- exactly the mechanism §10's own ProvisioningRepo path already uses for every caller today.

DESIGN WRITTEN: lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md new §11.10 (six subsections, §11.10.0-§11.10.6 open questions), added after §11.9.5 (the file's prior end, line 3109) -- did not fold into §11.2/§11.3/§11.6 in place, since this is a NEW, independently-diagnosed defect requiring its own re-derivation and rejected-alternatives record, matching this design's own established pattern for prior reworks (§9, §10.8, §11.9 are each their own numbered section for the same reason).

THE FIX (§11.10.2), stated signature-level only: split the current single `connection_wrap` local binding in provisioned_tenant!/1 (§11.6 item 2) into two separately-named closures -- `provision_wrap` (identical logic to today's connection_wrap: provision_via_shared_connection/1 when template == :clone and the shared-mode flag is set, else with_provisioning_repo/1 -- UNCHANGED, still used only for the provisioning call) and `teardown_wrap` (always &with_provisioning_repo/1, unconditionally, regardless of what provision_wrap resolved to). The on_exit/1 registration becomes `on_exit(fn -> teardown_wrap.(fn -> teardown(tenant.id, owner) end) end)` -- literally the same shape §10.3.2's ProvisioningRepo path already uses for every caller today, now applied unconditionally to teardown specifically. This directly narrows (not reverses) §11.3's prior 'teardown must close over the SAME dispatch decision as provisioning' instruction: that premise is still correct for why provisioning and the test body's OWN reads must share a connection (read-your-own-write, same-transaction visibility while the test is running) -- it does not extend to teardown, which runs strictly after the test's own reads are done and the provisioning connection's participation has ended, when the only property needed is 'sees committed rows in the same database.'

RE-VERIFIED SAFE against both prior hazards (§11.10.2's own subsections, re-derived not asserted): (1) ORIGINAL ISS-0113/ISS-0480 hazard -- with_provisioning_repo/1's Sandbox.mode/2 call has never, in any iteration, targeted Letflow.Repo; it targets ProvisioningRepo exclusively, so routing teardown through it is reuse of an already-safety-verified mechanism, not a new call to audit. (2) Mechanism 4 (§9.2/§11.9) -- a mode call against a DIFFERENT repo's pool cannot check in a connection it does not own (one ownership-manager process per pool, confirmed against provisioning_repo.ex's own moduledoc); additionally, by the time on_exit/1 fires there is no longer any in-flight uncommitted work on Letflow.Repo left to disrupt, since the owning test process has already exited.

HARDENING (§11.10.3, secondary to the root-cause fix, explicitly NOT a substitute for it): widen guarded/2 and log_teardown/3's rescue-only clauses to also `catch :exit, _` with the same fallback value, matching INV-F-10's stated intent for the failure shape this rework discovered. Explicitly specified that teardown/2's own DROP SCHEMA/delete_all statements must NOT be wrapped in any guarded/2-style boundary -- they are load-bearing cleanup, not a diagnostic read, and swallowing their failure would silently orphan tenant schemas/rows, which is worse than today's loud failure and is exactly the anti-pattern docs/anti-patterns.md warns against.

VERIFICATION SPECIFIED (§11.10.4) beyond re-running §11.7 items 1-6 (backfill_test.exs must reach 5/5, context_test.exs must reach 11/11 -- full closure, not partial improvement): an explicit NEW post-teardown state check (from a separate test running after, since on_exit fires before the next sync-queue test starts) asserting the schema is actually gone from information_schema.schemata AND the Registration/Tenant tracking rows are actually gone -- because a green test run alone cannot distinguish 'teardown ran to completion' from 'a swallowed failure silently skipped it,' which is exactly the gap a guarded/2 boundary could hide if misapplied. Also specified a check that the widened §11.10.3 boundary does not get confused with, or extended to, the load-bearing cleanup statements themselves.

What ELIXIR-DEV implements (§11.10.5, signatures only): (1) tenant_fixture.ex provisioned_tenant!/1 -- split connection_wrap into provision_wrap/teardown_wrap as above, @spec unchanged; (2) guarded/2 -- body changes from the current one-line `fun.() rescue _exception -> degraded` shorthand to an explicit try/rescue/catch form adding `catch :exit, _reason -> degraded`, signature/arity/return-contract unchanged; (3) log_teardown/3's trailing rescue clause -- identical widening; (4) teardown/2's own body -- explicitly UNCHANGED, no guarded/2 wrapping added; (5) no change to provision_via_shared_connection/1, with_provisioning_repo/1, ProvisioningRepo, TenantTemplate (including §11.9's ensure_template!/0 fix, untouched), config/test.exs, or scripts/test_parallel.sh.

Two new open questions recorded, not silently resolved: OQ-14 (whether routing every async:false caller's teardown through ProvisioningRepo's pool_size-2 pool raises peak concurrent checkouts beyond §10.2.2's existing headroom arithmetic -- argued it should not, since async:false tests never run concurrently with each other and each checkout is brief, but flagged for TEST-RUNNER's full-suite run to confirm empirically rather than asserted as proven); OQ-15 (the widened guarded/2 catches :exit broadly, any reason, matching rescue's own already-broad any-exception precedent -- recorded as a deliberate breadth choice consistent with this module's existing idiom, not an oversight, in case a future reader wants a narrower match).

No implementation code written -- design document only, signatures/structure/behavior described in prose, matching every prior section's own convention in this file. test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and test/support/tenant_template.ex were read in full but not modified by this handoff.
